rulings.challenge_claim: The three-site recurrence of the quoted-objection construction is asserted beside a byte tier label, but the shared wording holds only at the consonantal-skeleton tier; and one closing gloss reaches past the run it is attached to.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, both halves stand. The construction spliced at oshb:Jer.33.10, אֲשֶׁר֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים (byte), sweeps to 1 verse at byte tier and 1 at accent_stripped -- oshb:Jer.33.10 alone, the meteg surviving the accent strip -- and to 3 verses only at the consonantal-skeleton tier (oshb:Jer.32.36, oshb:Jer.32.43, oshb:Jer.33.10). The two earlier sites carry a byte-distinct pointing, אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte), which sweeps to 2 verses by itself at byte tier. So the 3-verse digit and the third-and-last ordinal are both true, but only at the weakest tier -- a contiguous consonantal substring search with its own named hazard -- while the sole tier label in the sentence sits on the adjacent single-verse splice. A recurrence claim owes its own tier at write time, and an ordinal exclusivity riding on an unlabelled digit makes the omission material rather than cosmetic; that is why this settles at medium and not low. The second item is a distinct defect and also holds: the closing splice עַל יְדֵ֥י מוֹנֶ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.33.13, byte) covers the counter's-hands clause and the divine-speech tag only, while the English paired with it also renders the flock-passing clause, whose Hebrew, עֹ֣ד תַּעֲבֹ֧רְנָה הַצֹּ֛אן (oshb:Jer.33.13, byte), stands outside the run -- gloss extent exceeding splice extent. Neither seam is touched: both onsets are verse-initial divine-mouthed koh-amar formulas, and the span's mark set (setumah at oshb:Jer.33.11 and oshb:Jer.33.13, paseq at oshb:Jer.33.10 and oshb:Jer.33.12, single-witness WLC, count-only) is disclosed in full and matches the inventory.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: label the recurrence with its own tier -- state the 3-verse digit and the third-and-last ordinal as a consonantal-skeleton sweep, and keep the byte label attached only to the oshb:Jer.33.10 splice it belongs to. Test the cure by re-sweeping the exact pointed run at the tier named: the sentence must not survive if the sweep at that tier fails to return both the digit and the ordinal. boundary_rationale: re-cut the closing pairing at oshb:Jer.33.13 so gloss extent equals splice extent -- either extend the splice back through the flock-passing clause or shorten the English to what the quoted run holds. Test: every curly-quoted rendering must be re-derivable from the splice standing beside it, with no word of English left unsupported by the Hebrew quoted.

rulings.challenge_claim: The internal-seam argument misplaces what the formula at 33:17 governs; the structured signal key files the days-are-coming formula under the date-frame family, which the byte-swept date census excludes; and a paseq inside the span goes undisclosed while the same verse's setumah is cited.
rulings.grounds: All three hold on the bytes. First: oshb:Jer.33.17 opens כִּי כֹ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.33.17, byte), a ki-subordinated formula, and what follows it is the throne guarantee alone, לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֣ת לְדָוִ֔ד אִ֕ישׁ יֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל כִּסֵּ֥א בֵֽית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.33.17, byte) -- “David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel” (web:Jer.33.17). The turn to the priesthood falls one verse later at וְלַכֹּהֲנִים֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.33.18, byte), which opens on a plain waw and carries no speech formula at all. The row states twice -- in the boundary field and again in the rejected alternative -- that the guarantee turns from throne to altar at verse 17; that is byte-false at the coordinate named, so the rival being declined is described at the wrong verse and under a device that does not stand there. The one-unit reading survives: no addressee or frame-owner change falls anywhere between oshb:Jer.33.14 and oshb:Jer.33.18. Second: the machine-readable key files הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.33.14, byte) under the date-frame family, but the byte-swept date and reign header object holds 19 classified candidate sites and oshb:Jer.33.14 is not among them; the formula is a temporal prophetic onset, sweeping to 5 verses at byte tier and 15 at the consonantal tier, not a dated reign header. Third: the inventory records a paseq seg at oshb:Jer.33.16 inside the span and it is cited nowhere, while that same verse's setumah is cited -- the span's mark set is therefore not fully disclosed, and the asymmetry sits inside a field that has already engaged both layers elsewhere in this part.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: move the throne-to-altar turn to oshb:Jer.33.18 and say that verse opens on a plain waw with no speech formula; describe the oshb:Jer.33.17 device as a ki-subordinated koh-amar introducing the throne guarantee. Test: the rival's verse and its device must both be re-derivable from the bytes at the coordinate named, and the sentence must fail if the formula quoted does not stand at that verse. observed_substrate_signals: replace the date_frame key carrying the days-are-coming formula with a non-date onset key. Test: every date_frame key in the row must resolve to a site the classified date and reign header census actually holds. device_notes: add the paseq at oshb:Jer.33.16 as a count-only, single-witness disclosure. Test: for each layer the field engages, every coordinate the inventory records inside the span is named.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closing comparison at 33:22 is named as a second analogy from the day-night covenant, but the bytes draw it from the uncountable host of heaven and the immeasurable sand of the sea; and the conditional splice at 33:20 stops short of the words its English renders.
rulings.grounds: Both hold. oshb:Jer.33.22 opens on its own protasis, אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יִסָּפֵר֙ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְלֹ֥א יִמַּ֖ד ח֣וֹל הַיָּ֑ם (oshb:Jer.33.22, byte), and only then reaches the apodosis the row splices; the comparandum is creation order -- “As the army of the sky can't be counted, and the sand of the sea can't be measured” (web:Jer.33.22) -- not the covenant of oshb:Jer.33.20 and oshb:Jer.33.21, and the words carrying it lie wholly outside the quoted run, so the mischaracterisation cannot be caught from the splice alone. Same class, second instance: the conditional splice at oshb:Jer.33.20 ends at the first covenant noun while the English paired with it runs on through the day covenant and the night covenant, whose Hebrew, הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י הַלָּ֑יְלָה (oshb:Jer.33.20, byte), is outside the splice. Both are prose-and-pairing defects, not seam defects, which is why this settles at low: the bounding formulas at oshb:Jer.33.19 and oshb:Jer.33.23 are verse-initial members of the 21-verse word-event set (the third and fourth of the four such onsets standing in this two-chapter block, after oshb:Jer.32.26 and oshb:Jer.33.1), no addressee or frame-owner change falls inside the span, and the span's single setumah at oshb:Jer.33.22 is disclosed and matches the inventory with no paseq and no variant note anywhere in the span.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: re-describe the closing comparison at oshb:Jer.33.22 as drawn from the uncountable host of heaven and the immeasurable sand of the sea, and either extend the splice to carry that protasis or drop the same-covenant characterisation entirely; re-cut the oshb:Jer.33.20 pairing so the English stops where the splice stops, or extend the splice through the night covenant. Test: each characterisation of a comparison must be re-derivable from the bytes of the verse it names, and each curly-quoted rendering from the splice beside it alone -- the original fails both tests as written.

rulings.challenge_claim: The declared false positive on the in-field variant disclosure is refuted: the form-exact recurrence sweep lands on the qere at one of its two sites, and the field carrying that sweep gives no variant disclosure.
rulings.grounds: The digit re-derives independently and the exclusivity holds: the quoted clause sweeps to exactly 2 verses at byte, accent_stripped and consonantal tiers alike -- oshb:Jer.32.44 and oshb:Jer.33.26 -- so nothing in the claim's arithmetic is wrong. What is wrong is its disclosure. At oshb:Jer.33.26 the matched run is the pointed qere with the unpointed ketiv standing immediately before it in the same clause, כִּֽי אשוב אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.33.26, byte), while the other site carries no variant note at all, כִּֽי אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.32.44, byte); the inventory records one variant note at oshb:Jer.33.26 and none at oshb:Jer.32.44 (single-witness WLC). The disposition treated as a false positive is the warning that a Hebrew quote in the device field binds to a variant-bearing verse with no variant disclosure in that field, and that warning is exactly true: a form-exact claim asserted across one marked and one unmarked site is the guarded hazard, and the marks were read in the boundary field but not in the field that makes the claim. The declared disposition therefore does not hold. The wider-construction texture standing at oshb:Jer.33.11 is not owed against this row: the claim is explicitly to the exact inflected form and is true at that scope, so severity settles at low -- an incomplete disclosure, not a false claim.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the ketiv/qere disclosure at oshb:Jer.33.26 beside the recurrence sentence, naming that the matched form is the qere, that the unpointed ketiv stands immediately before it, and that the sweep's other site carries no note (single-witness WLC). Re-mark that flag's disposition from false positive to accepted. Test: every Hebrew quote binding to a verse the variant inventory records must carry the variant disclosure inside its own field, not only elsewhere in the row -- the original passes nowhere else and fails here.

rulings.challenge_claim: A byte-true release-term chain runs across this row's own closing seam and is disclosed in neither prose field.
rulings.grounds: The cohesion object is byte-true. The release noun stands inside the span in the very clause naming the covenant this row narrates, לִקְרֹ֥א לָהֶ֖ם דְּרֽוֹר (oshb:Jer.34.8, byte), and again twice past the seam at oshb:Jer.34.15 and oshb:Jer.34.17; the consonantal sweep returns 3 verses book-wide and all 3 sit in this chapter, so the term is attested on both sides of the cut and nowhere else in the book. A byte-true device straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and neither prose field names it. The cut itself is untouched and the remedy is disclosure, not a respan: oshb:Jer.34.12 is a whole verse opening on the formula itself, וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.34.12, byte), a verse-initial member of the 21-verse word-event set, which is the book's primary macro-seam device -- hence low. Everything else in the span verifies: the header at oshb:Jer.34.8 is the prose-sermon superscription shape, the closing variant pair is quoted as the bytes have it, and the front petuchah at oshb:Jer.34.7 and the closing setumah and variant note at oshb:Jer.34.11 all match the inventory under the right type (single-witness WLC). Separately observed and not raised against this row: the device field attaches a byte tier label to bare coordinates where no Hebrew run is quoted -- the same shape recurs at oshb:Jer.34.11, oshb:Jer.34.16, oshb:Jer.34.22, oshb:Jer.35.5, oshb:Jer.35.11, oshb:Jer.35.15 and oshb:Jer.35.16 across this part, so it is a sweep-class candidate rather than a one-row fix.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add one sentence disclosing the release term inside the span at oshb:Jer.34.8 and its two occurrences past this row's close at oshb:Jer.34.15 and oshb:Jer.34.17 (sweep: 3 verses, all in this chapter), and state that the verse-initial word-event onset at oshb:Jer.34.12 carries the cut against that cohesion. Because one seam is at stake, this and the facing disclosure on the unit opening at oshb:Jer.34.12 are ONE paired edit, not two independent ones. Test: the sentence must name the swept object, its unit and its digit, and must fail if the term proves attested outside this chapter. Corpus-wide order candidate (separate sweep, not this row's work order): strip or re-site the byte tier labels attached to bare coordinates in device_notes throughout this part, so a tier label always names a quoted run.

rulings.challenge_claim: The structured signal key marks the 34:12 word-event formula as the book's non-initial occurrence, which the verse bytes and the book-wide census both contradict; the parashah citations doing pivot work in the boundary field stand without their witness disclosure; and the release-term chain crosses the row's opening seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: All three items are confirmed on the bytes; the severity settles at medium, not high. Position: oshb:Jer.34.12 is a whole verse of eight words opening on the formula itself, וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.34.12, byte). The byte-swept census carries this verse among the 21 sites of that shape, records 20 of them verse-initial, and reserves the non-initial label for exactly one site elsewhere in the book, where a ten-days temporal clause precedes the formula. Filing this site under the non-initial term asserts a second exception against a byte-proven single-site fact, inside the machine-readable field, and contradicts the row's own boundary prose, which states the position correctly and quotes the full verse. High overstates it precisely because of that: no boundary moves -- a verse-initial onset is if anything the more ordinary tier-1 warrant -- and no prose digit or exclusivity is corrupted; what is defective is a false structured label, which is medium. Second: the setumah at oshb:Jer.34.16 and the closing petuchah at oshb:Jer.34.22 are both cited inside the field carrying the boundary argument with no single-witness naming, while that disclosure appears only in the device field; this layer requires the disclosure on every citation, and the first of the two sits at exactly the pivot the row declines to cut. Third: the release term reaching this span from oshb:Jer.34.8 (sweep: 3 verses, all in this chapter) crosses this row's opening seam undisclosed -- the facing half of the same seam's cohesion gap. What verifies: both variant pairs are byte-exact at oshb:Jer.34.11 and oshb:Jer.34.17, the span's mark set is otherwise complete and correctly typed, and the refusal to cut at the therefore-clause is sound, the same divine mouth carrying the formula on both sides of oshb:Jer.34.17.
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the non-initial word-event key with the verse-initial key of the same shape. Test: the census's non-initial label may stand on exactly one row in the book and only at the site the census names; the position must be re-derived from the verse's own first word before the key is written -- the original fails on the verse's first word. boundary_rationale: add single-witness naming and the mark type to both parashah citations in that field, or drop them there and leave the layer to the device field. Test: every parashah citation in every field names its single witness and its type, petuchah never conflated with setumah. device_notes: disclose the release-term chain crossing the front seam from oshb:Jer.34.8 into oshb:Jer.34.15 and oshb:Jer.34.17 -- ONE paired edit with the facing disclosure on the unit closing at oshb:Jer.34.11, not two.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two byte-checkable naming lapses: the armies fled from are Chaldean in both witnesses rather than Babylonian, and the ancestor whose charge the unit turns on stands in two attested spellings inside this span, undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The first lapse is real; the second is a true byte observation wrongly framed as a lapse of the same class, so the challenge is refined rather than upheld whole. First: oshb:Jer.35.11 reads מִפְּנֵי֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּמִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֣יל אֲרָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.35.11, byte) -- for fear of the army of the Chaldeans and for fear of the army of Aram. The Babylon token stands once in that verse and only inside the royal title, נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֮ (oshb:Jer.35.11, byte), and the Babylon token, its directional form and the Chaldeans token are separate count objects that are never blended. Calling the armies Babylonian blends two of them at the single place in the span where the distinction is visible, and both witnesses read otherwise: “for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians” (web:Jer.35.11). Second: the ancestor does stand in two attested spellings in span -- the short form יוֹנָדָ֨ב (oshb:Jer.35.6, byte), which sweeps to 3 verses at the consonantal tier (oshb:Jer.35.6, oshb:Jer.35.10, oshb:Jer.35.19), and the long form יְהוֹנָדָ֤ב (oshb:Jer.35.8, byte), which sweeps to 4 (oshb:Jer.35.8, oshb:Jer.35.14, oshb:Jer.35.16, oshb:Jer.35.18), both confined to this chapter. But the duty to name a name form is triggered by a digit, a form claim or an exclusivity claim about the name, and this row hangs none: it quotes the ancestor inside a verse splice and counts nothing. Recording the variance would improve the row; its absence is not a defect, and pairing it with the token blend overstates it. Neither item moves a boundary: the header at oshb:Jer.35.1 is a byte-identical member of the prose-sermon superscription shape, the closing seam rests on the verse-initial word-event onset at oshb:Jer.35.12, and the span's marks -- the preceding petuchah at oshb:Jer.34.22, the closing petuchah at oshb:Jer.35.11 and the count-only paseq at oshb:Jer.35.5 -- all match the inventory (single-witness WLC), with no variant note owed anywhere in the span.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: name the armies by the tokens the verse carries -- the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram -- and leave the Babylon token to the royal title where it actually stands. Test: every nation-token characterisation must be re-derivable from the tokens standing in the verse cited, with the Babylon token, the directional form and the Chaldeans token never blended; the original fails on the one verse where all of them are in view. No work order issues on the name-form half: if the spelling variance is added at all, it must name both attested spellings with their own digits and units, and it must not be recorded as a repair.

rulings.challenge_claim: The word-event key marks a verse-initial formula as the book's non-initial occurrence; one divine-title key collapses two byte-distinct koh-amar stacks the span carries side by side; the count-only paseq citation carries the wrong digit; and the row gives no disclosure for keeping a koh-amar judgment address under the symbolic-act category.
rulings.grounds: Three of the four items hold and one is refuted, and one supporting digit is attached to the wrong object. Position: oshb:Jer.35.12 is a whole verse opening on the formula, וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.35.12, byte); the census carries it among the 21 sites of that shape, 20 verse-initial, with the single non-initial site standing elsewhere in the book -- so the non-initial key is byte-false here, exactly as at the sibling site closing at oshb:Jer.34.22, and the cure is the same. Title blending: upheld. The title at the first formula is the full signature stack, יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.35.13, byte), a member of the 32-verse object; the title at the therefore-clause is a different stack, יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.35.17, byte), which sweeps to 1 verse at byte tier and 3 at the consonantal tier (oshb:Jer.35.17, oshb:Jer.38.17, oshb:Jer.44.7) and is not a member of the 32-verse object at all. Correction to the challenge's own arithmetic: the 5-verse digit does not belong to that five-word run -- it belongs to the shorter God-of-Armies title, יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י צְבָאוֹת֙ (oshb:Jer.35.17, byte), which sweeps to 5 verses at the consonantal tier (oshb:Jer.5.14, oshb:Jer.15.16, oshb:Jer.35.17, oshb:Jer.38.17, oshb:Jer.44.7); naming the object before the digit is what separates them, and the blending finding stands under either object. The row's own prose quotes and renders both titles distinctly and byte-exactly, so the blend is confined to the single structured key, which is where it must be cured. Paseq digit: upheld -- the inventory records two segs at oshb:Jer.35.15 and the citation names one, and under a count-only convention the digit is the whole content of the citation. Unit type: refuted. The operative-category law permits a per-bytes deviation from the operative category on a one-sentence disclosure; it does not demand a disclosure for using the operative category itself. This span is the interpretation half of a symbolic-act report whose command, performance and interpretation default to one unit except where a tier-1 seam intervenes -- which is precisely what the word-event onset did here -- and the row's own literature type names it as that interpretation. No deviation is asserted, so no deviation sentence is owed. New finding, unraised on this row: the setumah at oshb:Jer.35.16 is cited in the boundary field with no single-witness naming and no type disclosure of its own, and the same citation in the device field carries no witness tag either -- the same class already visible at the sibling site.
rulings.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the non-initial word-event key with the verse-initial key of the same shape; and split the single divine-title key into two, one for the full signature stack at oshb:Jer.35.13 and one for the God-of-Armies stack at oshb:Jer.35.17. Test: the non-initial label may stand at exactly one site book-wide, and each title key must resolve to one byte-distinct attested stack -- no key covering two, and no digit carried without its object named. device_notes: correct the paseq citation at oshb:Jer.35.15 to the digit the inventory records (2 segs), keeping it count-only with no intra-verse position; and add single-witness naming plus the mark type to the setumah citation at oshb:Jer.35.16 in both fields that cite it. Test: every count-only citation carries the inventory's own digit, and every parashah citation names its single witness and its type. No work order issues on unit_type.
